reason: Self-* AEIS layer (autonomy_controller, evolution_tracker, self_evolution, self_healing_orchestrator, integration_controller, self_limitation, self_observation, self_preservation, self_explanation, evidence_pack, adaptation_engine, explanation_engine, improvement_queue, autonomy_stages) — 14 SQLite-backed modules. Each tracks its OWN internal lifecycle/limit/healing state. Tables are platform-runtime (autonomy_state, evolution_steps, healing_sessions, sylion_rate_events) — not domain payload other modules query. The published Evidence Pack lives in sylion/governance/evidence_spine + sylion/aeis/evidence_pack stays as a writer adapter. Stays as-is; W15 OSDK is consumed FROM here, not OF here.

Advisor (W13) — 13 sub-services (engine, funding, history, mobile_gateway, orchestration_config, preferences, pricing, role_resolver, scaling, subscription, variants, actions, events) already on PostgreSQL via dedicated `advisor_layer.sql` schemas (advisor_engine, advisor_funding, advisor_history, advisor_pricing, advisor_preferences, advisor_actions, advisor_outbound, advisor_subscription, advisor_scaling, advisor_orchestration, advisor_evidence, advisor_events). Heavy CRUD on AdvisorCard / Recommendation / FundingMatch / PreferenceKey — perfect OSDK candidates. Already half-way to W15 (PG done, schemas defined).

W14 Testing — DIRECTLY targeted by §6.3 lift to W15 (25 ontology objects manifested as YAML, SQLite -> PG, 10-step migration with rollback). Every submodule (charter, findings, agent_theater, auto_repair_controller, loop_governor, merge_guard, release_rail, self_audit, simulation/, branches/, personas/, guardians/, demo_projects/, actions/, ontology/, memory.py) imports from `aeis.testing.ontology.objects` and `aeis.testing.ontology.store`. This is THE canonical Class B example.

Empty placeholder (only __pycache__ subdirs for ontology/apps/deployment/terminal). This IS the v2 namespace into which W15-W18 will land. Currently no code, no manifests, no schemas — formally deprecated as a v1 module (becomes the W15 home).

103 *_routes.py files — almost every router queries domain objects (idea_vault, council, advisor, projects, governance, testing). Routes are thin wrappers over service-layer modules; once W15 generates REST + Python OSDK from manifests, ~70% of these routes become auto-generated. Backbone routes (auth_routes, health_routes, ws_routes, rbac_enforcement, rate_limit, router.py, app.py) stay; entity CRUD routes (idea_routes, projects_routes, council_routes, advisor_routes, testing_routes, etc.) refactor to use OSDK or get auto-generated.

Single-file module (stage_machine.py) holding 2 SQLite tables (autonomy_phase_state, autonomy_transitions). Internal state machine for autonomy phase transitions — used only by sylion/aeis. Not a domain object exposed to other layers. Stays.

7-file lab toolkit (attack_vectors, control_plane, core_network, evidence_writer, ran_lab, rf_isolation, ue_emulator) — each owns one tiny SQLite table for cellular/RAN test artifacts. Domain (cellular_evidence, ue_devices, attack_vectors) is unrelated to AEIS ontology and won't be queried via OSDK by other layers. Pure standalone test-rig domain — leave it as-is.

Heart of the cognitive stack — 21 modules with 30+ SQLite tables for first-class domain objects every other layer queries: ideas/idea_attachments/idea_lifecycle_log, chat_sessions/messages/attachments, evaluation_criteria/evaluations/evaluation_results, knowledge_entries/sources/links, feedback_categories/items/responses/ratings, registered_models/agents/runtime, plans/tasks, prompt_templates/versions, llm_calls, hallucination_checks/patterns. idea_vault alone is 973 LOC with 4 tables and is referenced by 55+ files. THE flagship Class B target — once OSDK exists, this is what powers W18 Operator Terminal and most W16 apps.
Single voting.py + __init__.py — pure algorithmic helpers (Borda/weighted vote math). No tables, no router, no ontology dependency. Stays as a math util.

Single docker_manager.py with 4 SQLite tables for container/k8s metadata (docker_containers, docker_images, k8s_pods, k8s_deployments). Infra-domain that overlaps W17 Deployment Plane scope, but the in-process lib stays — W17 will consume it via gRPC. Mark A; revisit at W17 G1.

Schema-registry tooling: dependency_graph, version_tracker, stub_manager, freeze_manager, generate_manifests, generate_stubs, event_validator, compatibility_checker — all build-time/CI. 3 small SQLite tables (sylion_dependencies, sylion_stub_registry, sylion_versions) are local indexes, not domain data. This module IS the meta-layer that W15 will largely replace, but until W15 G2 lands the existing tooling stays.

21 infrastructure modules: event_bus, event_backbone, nats_event_bus, manifest_loader, module_registry, lifecycle_gates, hot_swap, rollback_manager, version_manager, pipeline_controller, pipeline_config, build_state, code_snapshot, contract_registry, environment_orchestrator, evidence_spine, dependency_mapper, decision_gate_engine, health_monitor, bundle_assembler, auto_register. These are platform plumbing — event bus and registries underpin everything but aren't domain objects. Their tables (sylion_events, sylion_modules, decision_records, evidence_spine, lifecycle_stages) are runtime metadata. Stays unchanged; W15 sits on top of core, not inside it.

Migration / pool plumbing: migration.py, pg_migration.py, pg_migration_worker.py, pool.py, advisor_layer.sql, migrations/0001_w14_ontology.py. Once W15 owns the manifest-driven DDL (auto-generates tables from YAML), this hand-written migration scaffolding is the canonical example of duplicated functionality. The pool helpers stay (or move into W15 storage engine), the ad-hoc CREATE TABLE migrations get deleted in favor of W15 manifest-driven DDL.

Demo app for Factory Automation — 5 tables (factory_cabinets, factory_iomaps, factory_estops, factory_uploads, factory_interlocks) + own router + service. EXACTLY the kind of operational app W16 Apps Builder is meant to define declaratively from a manifest. Refactor target post-W16 G2.

Demo app — 4 tables (funding_applications, funding_attachments, funding_signatures, funding_submissions). Overlaps with sylion/funding_autopilot (which already owns funding_applications). One of these duplicates either becomes a W16 app or is deprecated.

Demo app — 4 tables (field_inspections, field_photos, field_signatures, field_offline_queue) + offline-capable mobile UX. Strong W16 app candidate (objects + workflow + automation manifest). Imports W14 ontology in __init__ (keeps ontology=true tag).
Demo CRM app — 3 tables (crm_contacts, crm_project_links, crm_audit_log). Trivial W16 ObjectListView + ObjectFormEditor app. Refactor post-W16 G2.
Demo portal — 3 tables (portal_projects, portal_comments, portal_submissions). Public-read object app — W16 candidate.

Demo marketplace — 4 tables (marketplace_skills, marketplace_dependencies, marketplace_scans, marketplace_reviews). Cross-cuts sylion/skills (which owns skills/executions). Likely W16 manifest app reading from /sylion/skills via OSDK.

Hardware lab toolkit (artifact_deployer, device_discovery, device_registry, test_harness) — 4 small tables for device fleet metadata. Domain orthogonal to AEIS ontology; mostly used by W14 hardware-lane testing scenarios. Stays standalone.

8 self-introspection helpers (circuit_breaker, code_bloat, config_drift, cost_envelope, cost_monitor, memory_footprint, performance_budget, runtime_perf). Each owns 1-2 SQLite tables of telemetry. Pure platform observability — no domain payload. Stays.

11 modules: adapter_bus, capacity_planner, connector_framework, deployment_orchestrator, execution_planner, job_runner, retry_orchestrator, task_scheduler, tool_registry, tool_runner, workflow_engine. Owns 25+ tables but they are all execution-runtime (jobs, workflows, retries, tools). These tables aren't queried from outside execution layer; they support the orchestrator. Stays unchanged; W15 will not lift workflow internals (decision: §3.3 / §6.2 W15 scope OUT for non-domain plumbing).

14 tables (funding_company_profiles, funding_company_documents, funding_programmes, funding_calls, funding_ideas, funding_projects, funding_matches, funding_partner_candidates, funding_outreach_messages, funding_applications, funding_submission_sessions, funding_approval_events, funding_alerts, funding_audit_events) + own router + service + governance bridge. Pure CRUD domain (FundingProgramme/Call/Idea/Match/Application objects). Top OSDK candidate alongside idea_vault and council. Note duplication with sylion/aeis/advisor/funding (advisor_funding.* tables) — should converge in W15.

30 modules covering Decision Gates, Human Gate, Council Hybrid, Compliance, Conflict Resolution, Evidence Spine, Policy Engine, Roles, Tickets, Rollback, Risk Scorer, Cascade Analyzer, Change Proposal/Merger. council_hybrid alone is 1123 LOC with 6 tables. These ARE the domain objects (CouncilSession, ParticipantVote, HumanGateRequest, Ticket, Policy, Risk Score) that W14 ontology cross-links to and W15 must expose via OSDK. Council/HG already have W14 wiring (council_session_id, hg_ticket_id on ReleaseDecision). Top P0 along with cognitive and aeis/testing.

6 gRPC server entrypoints (aeis_server, cognitive_server, core_server, eventbus_server, execution_server, governance_server). Pure transport adapters. Replaced/extended by W15 OSDK gRPC, but until then stays.
Auto-generated *_pb2.py / *_pb2_grpc.py files. Generated from sylion/contracts/proto/. Stays — W15 will generate its own stubs from manifests; existing stubs are independent.
Two helpers: cache.py and topology_templates.py. No tables, no router. Pure utility. Stays.
orchestrator.py + drift_detector.py — 3 tables (candidate_builds, integration_results, drift_records) for build/integration tracking. Platform plumbing similar to execution; not domain. Stays.

10 modules: book_generator, compact_layer, evidence_store, indexer, kanon_access, kb_adapter, self_model_store, retrieval, bootstrap. Tables are storage-layer caches/indexes/snapshots — text_index, compaction_records, stored_evidence, model_snapshots. The book/kanon entities are read-mostly artifact stores serving Cognitive — stays as a memory/index sublayer beneath W15. Domain payload (Idea, EvidencePack) is owned by cognitive/governance, not by memory.

11 telemetry modules (anomaly_detector, circuit_breaker, config_drift_detector, metric_aggregator, model_budget, model_performance, notification_engine, pipeline_monitor, self_healing, sla_monitor). 20+ tables but all platform-observability data (metric_points, observations, anomalies, sla_breaches, healing_incidents, breaker_events). Not domain payload. Stays — and is what W15/W17 query for health, not what gets lifted.
6-file telemetry hub (hub, log_aggregator, metrics_registry, pii_redactor, prometheus_exporter, tracing). No SQLite tables of its own (uses Prometheus / external sinks). Pure platform. Stays.

Tiny module (bridge, dispatcher, secrets, store) with 1 table (operator_mobile_devices). Mobile gateway scaffold — will gain weight when W18 Operator Terminal lands. Currently small and standalone enough to stay; revisit at W18 charter.
Single state_machine.py with 2 SQLite tables (pipeline_run_states, pipeline_state_log). Platform plumbing for pipeline state transitions. Stays.

23 SQLite tables in store.py + engine.py — Projects/Stages/Questions/Answers/Decisions/CanonEntries/Masterplans/Modules/Events/WorkerPool/CouncilMembers/CouncilVotes/HierarchyLayers/AutonomyConfig/AuditResults/CostLedger/Notifications/SkillReuseLog/BrainMemoryEntries/BrainEmbeddings/BrainPromptLibrary/BrainLoraDatasets/BrainLoraAdapters. This is the second-biggest single-store module in the codebase (134 references). Pure first-class domain — Project / Stage / Decision are core W15 objects.

6 modules (golden_set_registry, golden_set_runner, quality_gate, quality_gate_engine, regression_detector, test_runner) with 12 tables. golden_sets / golden_run_results / regression_alerts / test_suites / test_runs ALL have W14 ontology counterparts (EvaluationSuite, RegressionRun, TestSuite, TestRun, GoldenSet semantics). DUPLICATION CANDIDATE: post-W15 G3 (W14→W15 lift) the W14 ontology becomes single source of truth and these modules collapse into thin wrappers OR get deleted, with quality gate logic moving into sylion/aeis/testing. Top deprecation candidate alongside sim and db migrations.

8 modules (cft_runner, cutover_automation, cutover_controller, golden_set_manager, lpw_checkpoint, lpw_manager, orchestrator, rebuildability_framework) — 17 tables tracking cutover sessions and rebuild plans/snapshots. Rebuild governance is platform-runtime (LPW versions, snapshots, fidelity_results) — internal to the rebuildability subsystem. Some overlap with W14 ReleaseCandidate semantics but the cutover sequencing is operational, not data-modeled. Stays — W17 Deployment Plane will consume rebuild, not absorb it.

5 RF/SDR modules (capture_orchestrator, protocol_decoder, rf_safety_governor, sdr_gateway, signal_analyzer) — 6 tables for hardware lab telemetry. Standalone domain orthogonal to AEIS ontology. Stays.

24 modules (audit_query, audit_sink, audit_trail_aggregator, auth_provider, bootstrap_flow, bootstrap_init, evidence_signer, evidence_signer_v2, execution_guard, hardened_audit, key_store_unified, key_vault, phantom_wrapper, policy_engine, profile_manager, profile_swap, profile_unified, profiles, rbac, secret_provider, security_audit, security_profiles, session_broker, session_manager, sops_provider, startup_check). 30+ tables but all platform/security-runtime (auth_users, sessions, security_events, audit_log, keystore_entries, secrets). Per §2 v2 plan, security plane is out of W15 scope (deferred to potential W19). Stays unchanged; W15 OSDK does not lift API keys, sessions, or audit trail.

_db_shim.py duplicates 6 advisor_engine tables in flat (non-schema-qualified) names for sim/test fixtures. runner.py + scenarios.py + personas.py heavily overlap aeis/testing/personas + simulation engine. After W15 there is one canonical PG schema for advisor objects + W14 test ontology — this shim/runner should be deleted, scenarios consolidated into aeis/testing/simulation. Top deprecation candidate.

7 modules (catalog, demand_analyzer, demand_signal, executor, registry, runtime, schemas) with 8 tables. Domain (Skill, DemandSignal, SkillExecution, MarketplaceCatalogEntry) is exactly the W7 Skills Registry surface and is targeted by §8.2 Role Catalog extension. Lift to OSDK; W15 manifest replaces hand-written CREATE TABLEs.

Console UI/API surface (artifact_control, command_bus, console_api, console_ui, event_sourcing_store, process_canvas, readiness_engine, ws_gateway). Surface CONSUMES domain objects from cognitive/governance/advisor — its tables (intents, artifacts, canvases, ws_connections, event_stream) are operator-side platform state (commands issued, artifacts uploaded, sockets open). W18 Operator Terminal extends surface but doesn't lift these tables. Stays; W18 reads from W15 OSDK rather than rewriting surface.

Single provider_manager.py with 4 tables (vps_providers, vps_allocations, vps_certifications, vps_health_probes). VPS-fleet metadata; will be subsumed/extended by W17 Deployment Plane Node Registry, but until W17 G2 stays as-is (W17 will likely consume it via gRPC, not absorb the module).
7 modules (assignment, autoscaler, compact, monitor, registry, runtime, sandbox) with 3 tables (worker_registry, worker_assignments, build_topology). Pure runtime worker pool — platform infra. Stays.
